To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spin-state transitions are accompanied by anomalies in the thermal expansion coefficients of mixed cobaltites.

the spin-state transition temperatures in mixed rare-earth cobaltites are strongly dependent on the ionic radius and the concentration of the rare-earth ions, while for mixed chromites, they are dependent on the 1:1 ratio of cobalt and chromium ions in the crystal structure.
the spin-state transition temperatures of cobalt ions in the studied mixed RE cobaltite and cobaltites/chromites are strongly affected by cation substitution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of the cationic size, the ionic radius and the cationic substitution on the spin-state of the Co<sup>2+</sup> and Co<sup>4+</sup> ions in the mixed rare earth (RE) cobaltites and cobaltiteschromites.
the influence of cation substitution in the mixed cobaltites and cobaltites/chromites on their structural behaviour and the temperature of the spin-state transitions.
the influence of cation substitution (R, RR' = La, Pr and Nd, Sm, Gd) on spin-state transitions and phase behaviour in mixed RE cobalitites and cobaltiteschromites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin-state transition in mixed RE cobalitites and chromites is a cooperative phenomenon.
in all the mixed cobaltites, the spin state transition occurs at the same temperature as the maximum in the thermal expansion coefficient.
the spin state transitions in the cobaltites and the spin state transitions of the chromites are independent phenomena.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spin-state transitions are not only a function of the cation radius of rare earths, but they are also a function of the degree of the cation disorder.
in the case of cobaltites the spin-state transitions are not only a result of the change of the average ionic radius of the RE ions, but also depend on the type of the RE ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin state of Co3+ ions in the RE cobaltites can be controlled via the RE cation substitution and the cation size mismatch.
spin-state transitions in RE cobaltites are strongly affected by the size of the cations and by the ionic radii of the RE cations.
the spin state of Co3+ ions in the mixed cobaltites and cobaltites/chromites is determined by the competition between the cationic size and the ionic radius of rare-earth ions.
